fichas.title: Spectator stands
fichas.summary: Spectator stands may be fixed or mobile. Smaller installations with up to 10 seating rows can use a linear rise; other installations should use a parabolic rise. The page illustrates stepped seating, stands accessed from below or above, and a retractable stand. It recommends mobile catch nets behind goals, nets to close off upper-level seats and galleries during practice, and barriers on free sides. Access from below can reduce costs but may disrupt spectators and competitors.
uses: Protect spectators and the playing area

fichas.title: Sports-hall partition curtains
fichas.summary: The page shows partition-curtain arrangements between beams, a curtain at a beam with a sound-absorption recess, a curtain on both sides of a beam, and a pulley system mounted in a sound-absorbing recess inside a space frame. The wall and ceiling area beside the partition should be designed to prevent noise transfer when the partition is lowered. Curtain width depends on hall height and material thickness.
uses: Divide a sports hall into separate areas
Limit noise transfer when the partition is lowered

fichas.title: Changing and sanitary facilities
fichas.summary: Three proposed layouts show changing and sanitary facilities with separate corridors for people wearing street shoes and sports shoes. Showers should be immediately accessible from changing rooms, with a drying area between the wet shower area and the changing room. Where shower rooms are divided into two units, both units should connect to the adjacent changing rooms so either or both units can be used from either changing room. Teachers' rooms should be near changing rooms; the first-aid room should be on the same level as the sports area and may be integrated into the teachers' room. Shaded areas indicate floor areas laid with PVC grid mats.
uses: Separate circulation routes for street shoes and sports shoes
Provide changing, showering, washing, and drying facilities
Provide first aid near the sports area
